userPrompt: Does the GDPR let me keep customer data forever if I got consent once?
responseText:
**No.**

GDPR does **not** let you keep customer data forever just because you obtained consent once.

### Key rules
- **Consent must be informed and specific** (Art. 6(1)(a) and Art. 7). A vague “we may use your data for our business” or a one-time checkbox does **not** justify indefinite retention.
- **Storage limitation principle** (Art. 5(1)(e)): Personal data must be kept “no longer than is necessary for the purposes for which the personal data are processed.”  
  You must define **retention periods** or clear criteria for deletion. “Forever” or “as long as the customer exists” almost never satisfies this.
- Even with valid consent, you must still respect the data subject’s **right to withdraw consent at any time** (Art. 7(3)). Once withdrawn, you must stop processing and, in most cases, delete the data.
- You must also honour **erasure requests** (“right to be forgotten”, Art. 17) unless you have another lawful basis (e.g. legal obligation) that overrides it.

### Practical reality
- One-time consent is usually tied to a **specific purpose** (e.g. “send you our newsletter”). Once that purpose is fulfilled or the customer unsubscribes, you must delete or anonymize the data.
- If you want to keep data for other or future purposes, you need **fresh, granular consent** or another lawful basis (contract, legitimate interest with a proper balancing test, legal obligation, etc.).
- Supervisory authorities (and courts) routinely fine companies that treat consent as a perpetual license to hoard data.

**Bottom line**: Consent is not a “keep forever” card. You must set and enforce retention periods, delete data when it is no longer necessary, and make it easy for people to withdraw consent or request deletion.
